newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Ca. hydrocracker seen shut until June.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Ca. hydrocracker seen shut until June.

text.p: A hydrocracking unit which shut on January 21 at Tosco's refinery in Martinez, Calif. after an explosion, could remain out of service until June, about two months longer than initially forecast, said a source familiar with the plant.
"Initially we thought it was going to be out for one-and-a-half months, now it's probably going to be four," the source said.
He said the unit could restart "sometime in June."
The 32,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker, which turns fuel oil into gasoline, exploded and burned after a hydrocarbon line ruptured.
Initial expectations were for the unit to remain shut for between eight and 10 weeks, according to officials at the refinery.
The hydrocracker helps process 156,000 bpd of crude oil at the plant, which runs a combination of Alaskan crudes and heavier California grades.
"The big result is that heavy crude will be sloppy for a long while," up to three or four months, said a California crude oil trader.
He said the kind of damage sustained by the unit would likely require large replacement parts that take months to receive.

California heavy crude grades have fallen four times in less than two weeks, traders said, with California's largest producing field, Kern River, worth $15.75 a barrel this week, about $1.75 below late January levels.
Since the late January fire, Tosco has declared force majeure on near-term purchases of heavy crude, which total about 40,000 bpd for the Martinez plant, traders said.
